claims.claim: The importer pulls the patient's external history and maps allergies, medications, lab results, surgeries/procedures, vaccinations, and conditions/problems into the chart.
Imported data appears in the patient chart's ZusHealth section.

checks.note: the section is titled "Zus Health Data" (product spells it "Zus Health")

claims.claim: Provenance indicators on each row let you tell externally-sourced data from data entered in Medipyxis.

checks.note: a hardcoded badge cannot tell sources apart

claims.finding: Medications, allergies, labs, surgeries, and vaccinations show the row's real source. Conditions always show "Manual": ConditionItem hardcodes <ZusProvenanceBadge source="manual" /> (frontend/src/components/patient/ZusHealthDataSection.tsx:857), so conditions imported from Zus are labelled as entered by hand. Product defect.
claims.proposed_text: Medications, allergies, labs, surgeries, and vaccinations show a source badge on each row (Zus or Manual). Conditions do not yet show where they came from.
claims.reason: Conditions always show a Manual badge, so the badges do not tell sources apart on every row. Replaced by pm-zus-09.

claims.claim: A last-sync pill (green / yellow / red) shows how current the sync is.
Open the patient's chart, or start Pre-Charting for a visit, and click Pull (the ZusHealth import).

checks.note: Pre-Charting is the Precharting tab of the referral detail panel

claims.reason: Wording nit: the chart control is an icon button labelled (aria) "Pull from Zus Health" and the Precharting tab button reads "Pull from Zus Health", not "Pull"; the tab is "Precharting" in the referral detail panel.

claims.claim: Source badges mark what came from ZusHealth (except on conditions); the last-sync pill shows the sync time.
When you finalize a visit (Sign & Lock), Medipyxis sends the visit to ZusHealth automatically — there is no extra step.
claims.reason: Contribution only succeeds for facilities with a Zus builder configured (zus-contribute-visit throws ZusNotConfiguredError otherwise).

claims.claim: This is how Medipyxis participates in nationwide interoperability (TEFCA); the contribution reaches the patient's nationwide record via TEFCA.
claims.finding: The code sends FHIR resources to the Zus API (backend/supabase/functions/zus-contribute-visit/index.ts:1-13). Whether Zus forwards them to TEFCA is a Zus network property, not visible in Medipyxis code. The only TEFCA reference in the product is a network list in frontend/src/services/zusFhirImportService.ts:425. Cannot be confirmed from code.
claims.proposed_text: When a visit is signed, Medipyxis sends it to Zus Health automatically, so other providers on the Zus network can see the care you delivered.

proposed_checks.pattern: This is a GIVE-to-GET contribution: we share our clinical encounter data

claims.reason: Medipyxis code only sends the visit to the Zus API; reaching a nationwide TEFCA record is not visible in the product. TEFCA wording removed; pm-zus-07 covers the automatic send.

claims.claim: Medications, allergies, lab results, surgeries, and vaccinations show a source badge on each row: Zus for imported rows, Manual for rows entered in Medipyxis. Conditions currently show Manual on every row, including conditions imported from ZusHealth.
The automatic send happens only for patients who are linked to ZusHealth, at facilities that are connected to ZusHealth.
Always review imported data before relying on it clinically — external records can be incomplete or out of date.
